Hi Jules —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front and then a proposed next step:

- SDK: use go-sdk v0.9.2 (we've got a Go 1.20 compatibility note). Sample init below.
- Timeouts/retries: start with connect=250ms, read=2000ms, retries=3 with exponential backoff + jitter; increase read timeout for streaming.
- Rate limits: we recommend 100 rps steady per client initially with 3x burst allowance; SDK surfaces 429 with a Retry-After header, and there is a RetryPolicy helper.
- Cutover checklist: we maintain a sandbox->prod CSV (attached: cutover-checklist.csv) and a recommended staged ramp (10%/50%/100% over 24–48hr windows).

Proposed next step: quick handoff call where Monica (CSM) and one of our Implementation Engineers join to walk the MAP and run through the snippet. How does Tue 5/16 11am PT look?

Quick SDK snippet (Go):

package main

import (
  "context"
  "time"

  rwd "github.com/redwood/inference-go"
)

func main() {
  cfg := rwd.NewConfig("api-key-xxxx")
  cfg.Timeouts.Connect = 250 * time.Millisecond
  cfg.Timeouts.Read = 2000 * time.Millisecond
  cfg.RetryPolicy = rwd.ExponentialBackoff(3)

  client := rwd.NewClient(cfg)
  ctx := context.Background()
  // example call
  _, _ = client.Generate(ctx, rwd.GenerateRequest{Model: "redwood-large", Prompt: "Hello"})
}

I'll attach the CSV and the MAP. Monica — can you join the Tue slot if that works?

Best,
Markus Klein

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai To: Jules Park , markus_klein@redwood.ai Date: 2028-05-16T08:45:00-07:00 Subject: Re: Sandbox -> Prod: planning questions and timing On Tue, May 14, 2028 at 10:12 AM Jules Park wrote: > Thanks again for the demo last week — the runtime performance looked good... Hi Jules — Thanks for the MAP and the timing. I'm the CSM who will coordinate the implementation week. Quick operational notes that will help the kickoff: 1) Sandbox wiring checklist (high level): - Confirm API key and environment segregated keys (sandbox vs prod) - Warmup sequence: 50 synthetic requests over 10m window to prime caches - Telemetry hooks: pass request_id + route tag in headers (x-rwd-request-id, x-app-route) 2) Resiliency patterns we recommend in code (short example): - Use the SDK RetryPolicy helper and check for rwd.IsTransient(err) before retrying. - Surface 429 as transient but respect Retry-After; log quota usage to SLO dashboard. 3) Cutover ramp suggestion (conservative): - Day 0: smoke tests & acceptance on prod (no traffic) - Hour 0–6: 5% traffic (monitor latency, errors)
- Hour 6–24: 25% traffic if error rate < 0.5% - Day 2: 100% if steady-state metrics look good 4) Endpoint migration note: if you're switching from our legacy /v1/generate to /v2/stream, you will want to: - Update client init and confirm streaming handlers close connections on client disconnect - Use the provided sampling key to keep prefix caches warm during ramp I'll join Tue 5/16 11am PT with an implementation engineer (Vanessa Ortiz) and an internal runbook link. I'll add the HubSpot deal link and the MAP to the calendar invite. Monica Patel Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference monica_patel@redwood.ai
